segments.text: Euclid's Elements, Book One, Proposition Six. If two angles of a triangle are equal, the sides opposite the equal angles are also equal. Given triangle A B C with angle A B C equal to angle A C B, we prove that side A B equals side A C.

segments.text: Suppose side A B is unequal to side A C, and let A B be greater. From the greater A B, cut off segment D B equal to the lesser A C, by Proposition Three. Next, construct segment D C, by Postulate One.

subsegments.text: Suppose side A B is unequal to side A C, and let A B be greater. From the greater A B, cut off segment D B equal to the lesser A C, by Proposition Three.
Next, construct segment D C, by Postulate One.

segments.text: Now compare triangles D B C and A C B: since D B equals A C, B C is common, and angle D B C equals angle A C B, Side-Angle-Side congruence in Proposition Four proves that triangle D B C equals triangle A C B. But triangle D B C is less than triangle A C B — the part equal to the whole, violating Common Notion Five. Therefore side A B is not unequal to side A C; side A B equals side A C, as was required to prove.
